## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Samasūpakapaṭiggahaṇa* is the twenty-ninth training rule of the *Sekhiya* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It governs the monastic etiquette of food reception, specifically regulating that curries or bean sauces are accepted in the correct proportion relative to rice [SuttaCentral]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral span multiple Vinaya traditions. Within the Pali tradition, direct parallels exist in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sekhiya 29), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* and *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Sekhiya 29), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī *Parivāra* (Sekhiya 29) [SuttaCentral]. Across other early Buddhist schools, corresponding rules are found in the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya for monks and nuns (Sekhiya 42 and 43 respectively), the Chinese Dharmaguptaka Vinaya for monks and nuns (Sekhiya 28), and a Chinese translation associated with the Upāliparipṛcchā (Sekhiya 27) [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 62 matching passages across 20 Pali texts, primarily consisting of standard formulaic phrases shared with neighboring rules in the *Sekhiya* class—most extensively with Sekhiya 34, Sekhiya 27, Sekhiya 30, Sekhiya 31, Sekhiya 37, and Sekhiya 28—as well as the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* commentary [DharmaNexus]. All returned citations in the reference literature refer to verse 29 of the non-Buddhist philosophical treatise *Sāṅkhyakārikā* rather than this Vinaya rule.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
